author: DTrim99
body:
Two things — the files in the directory don't match, and PolicyEngine is doing exactly what you specified for Kentucky in taxsim #1026, which differs from the rule you describe here.

**File mismatch.** The txpydata PolicyEngine ran is a Kentucky couple with **$9,744** of pension (ages 63/52), and PE excludes all of it. But the Schedule M, joint.pdf, and sep-comb.pdf are the title's record — ~$69K pension, ages 51/63 — whose Schedule M shows the **$31,110** exclusion. So the form's $31,110 and PE's exclusion aren't for the same return.

**PE's Kentucky rule.** For a 69K couple, PE splits the pension **50/50** and lets each spouse exclude up to $31,110 — so it excludes **$62,220** (KY AGI = 103,000 − 62,220 = 40,780), not $31,110. That's the convention set in taxsim #1026: "TAXSIM's kytax caps the combined pension at $31,110 × nret, which equals a 50/50 split with the per-person cap — so KY splits 50/50 at every age rather than route to the older spouse." PE keys KY to a split-age of 0 for exactly that reason, so age never matters.

The rule you describe here — mixed-age (one <55, one ≥55) → all pension to the older, one $31,110 exclusion — gives **$31,110**, matching TaxAct but contradicting the #1026 kytax convention (nret = 2 → $62,220). They diverge only for couples with more than $31,110 of pension.

So which Kentucky treatment do you want going forward: the 50/50 / two-cap rule from #1026 (what PE and TAXSIM's kytax do), or the mixed-age-to-older / single-cap rule here (what TaxAct does)? If it's the latter, I'll take KY off the 50/50 special-case — just confirm, since it reverses #1026. And if you can re-post the 69K txpydata to match the PDFs, I'll run it through to confirm.
